description_full: Turk Altin Isletmeleri A.S. engages in the gold mining operations in Turkey. It owns and operates seven mines in the regions of Ovacik-Bergama-Izmir, Çukuralan-Izmir, Kaymaz-Eskisehir, Mastra-Gümüshane, and Himmetdede-Kayseri. The company was formerly known as Koza Altin Isletmeleri A.S. and changed its name to Turk Altin Isletmeleri A.S. in November 2025. Turk Altin Isletmeleri A.S. was incorporated in 1989 and is headquartered in Ankara, Turkey.
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $132K ranks in the bottom quartile among Basic Materials peers. Each employee generates $9K of free cash flow annually. R&D investment of 9% of revenue (moderate) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: TURK ALTIN ISLETMELERI A S is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $2.4B market cap on $336M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -14% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -5.2pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 43%.

The business throws off $22M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.94× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sect: Its 22% operating margin runs 13pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.68x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 221 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 70% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 26% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 29% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 69% and a beta of 0.20, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -1.07 vs 5y -0.10), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $2K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 0% in the 2020 crash and 0% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $1.85 (margin of safety -299%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 12%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $1.68 to $2.09 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Basic Materials peers: P/FCF 107.2 vs 22.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 0.9% (below the risk-free rate).
The price implies 27.2% annual cash-flow growth, 37pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 9% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.28).
It runs a 43% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.94x.
ROE of 10% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.1x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $366.3M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 15.9, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -14.5% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 84% of profits supports about 7.7% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 0%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.4% (1.4% in dividends).
people: With about 2,550 employees, each generates about $132K of revenue, 0.2x the Basic Materials median.
That works out to $9K of free cash flow per employee.
